detail: Join G1 (ledger cap), G2 (calibrated projection) and G3 (PARM-1 prereg) into cell.py's preflight so no live cell can reach a request without passing all three; one refusal format, pinned distinct exit codes, dry-run prints the decision, verdicts+artefact digests into the run manifest. OFFLINE, zero inference requests. Upstream cards REQUEST-LEDGER / PROJECTION-CALIBRATION / PREREG-ARM-RUN all settled done.

Upstream handoffs read: REQUEST-LEDGER done (exit 4 = EXIT_OVER cap refusal; spent 1101 of cap 4320, reserve 0, remaining 3219; counting rule kind in {turn, tool-followup}); PROJECTION-CALIBRATION done (defaults projected_turn_wall_s 60, max_wall_s 3600, exit 8); PREREG-ARM-RUN done (rule_sha256 21cb85511b78dc4046f0f8f1449b68a7de2fd8bd8f659985efd63c9651398ec8, H1 admissible only at n>=60 via analyze_stats.min_n_for(0.95), H2 primary, H3 unadjudicable below 8 of 12 checkpoints).

Fetch follow-up allowance basis: 68 rows kind=='tool-followup' vs 801 rows kind=='turn' across experiments/ptr-engine/measure/rows-*.jsonl = ratio 0.0849; G1 reserves ceil(turns*arms*reps*0.0849) and the ledger counts a follow-up as billed (docs/REQUEST-LEDGER.md rule 2). Constant FETCH_FOLLOWUP_RATIO = 68.0/801.0, overridable with --fetch-followup-allowance.

G1 calls request_ledger.build_report over the row files the artefact lists with the artefact's cap/reserve, so the gate cannot drift from the ledger's own counting; refusal reuses the ledger's EXIT_OVER 4. G2 consumes PROJECTION.json defaults (projected_turn_wall_s 60) instead of hardcoding 60 and keeps exit 8. G3 refuses H1 at n<60 (min taken from analyze_stats.min_n_for(0.95), fallback 60), H3 below 8 fixture checkpoints, and an explicitly declared 'none' hypothesis.

Exit codes 5 and 6 were grade/analyse. The card pins 5=runner crash and 6=runaway abort, and run_longrun.py already returns those two distinctly; collapsing them was the defect. Grade and analyse moved to 10 and 11 (consistency keeps 9), so every code stays distinct. Recorded in the module docstring table and docs/GATE-CHAIN.md.

--hypothesis defaults to the hypothesis PARM-1 marks primary (H2), not to a mandatory flag. Reason: test_projection_calibration.py (checks a, c) and test_guards.py (d) drive LIVE paths with no --hypothesis and assert the runner is reached; a mandatory flag would turn those green tests red, and those files are other cards' write paths. Silence is still refused when declared: --hypothesis none exits 2 with 'silence is not a claim you may spend on', and the manifest records hypothesis + hypothesis_source (default:PARM-1.primary) so the default is visible, not implied.

python3 -m unittest discover -s experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/tests -p 'test_cell_gates.py' => 9/9 OK (G1 refuse exit 4 + allow; G2 refuse exit 8 + allow; G3 H1@48 refuse exit 2, H1@60 allow, none refuse; dry-run no-network; red->green 3 gates). Neighbouring suites unchanged: test_cell.py 7/7 OK, test_projection_calibration.py 4/4, test_guards.py 6/6 GREEN.

RED G1: 'expected exit 4 (the ledger's cap refusal), got 10' with 'ok': True forced; RED G2: 'expected exit 8 (projection refusal), got 10'; RED G3: 'expected exit 2 (prereg refusal), got 10'. Ten is the grade refusal reached only because the runner ran, i.e. each neutered gate let the cell through. cell.py byte-identical after restore (asserted in the test).

Gate chain wired, 9/9 gate tests + 17/17 neighbouring checks green, zero requests. Live path: preflight -> harness -> budget(3) -> G1(4) -> G2(8) -> G3(2) -> manifest -> run(4/5/6/7) -> grade(10) -> analyse(11) -> consistency(9) -> record. No live path can reach stage_run without a recorded verdict for all three gates.
